notes: litert-community/WeVisOne-VL-4B: WeVisOne-VL-4B_int4.litertlm, the repo's file for a GPU (its file for a CPU is WeVisOne-VL-4B_int8.litertlm), a LiteRT-LM fast_vlm conversion of tencent/WeVisOne-VL-4B (apache-2.0; WeChat Vision, Tencent; built on Qwen3-VL; converted from the float32 release at revision 4a7bed92, whose weights the current bfloat16 release 6b44a458 holds) — detection, referring, pointing, counting and OCR answers as <0>…<1000> coordinate tokens. These are the file's bytes of 2026-11-12: re-packed with LiteRT external weights from the bytes of the earlier records (0.19.1/2026-11-10/wevisone-vl-4b-int4__galaxy-s26.json, 1c14c17a7e8bd688…), the same weight bytes; an Android GPU needs LiteRT-LM 0.19.0 or later (the v0.18.0 and v0.18.1 Android builds crash (SIGSEGV) while the GPU engine is being built, LiteRT-LM#3986), and the earlier bytes stay at Hub revision ee03d010. Mac rows: one window on 2026-11-12 (12:05:51–12:16:11 JST), PyPI litert-lm 0.19.1, GPU (WebGPU, the vision encoder on the GPU) and CPU (XNNPACK, the decoder with the runtime's default 4 threads, the vision encoder on the CPU); the card prints the CPU rows as speed only (this file's answers were not checked on a CPU); three processes per row, one at a time, no cache files, both files held open and resident in memory. The picture process sends a second message in the same conversation ('Answer again in the same format.') that is timed only: LiteRT-LM 0.19.1 feeds the previous answer's stop token with a zero embedding from a conversation's second message on (files with an EMBEDDER section). Pictures are stretched to 512 x 512 before they are sent. Landed 2026-11-12: this file's bytes went up in litert-community/WeVisOne-VL-4B commit b4ed353a77452ae99a6eb102d4888491979d2b0e (2026-11-12 02:01:43 UTC = 2026-11-12 11:01:43 JST, both files with external weights, the card and MEASUREMENTS.md), the rows below in commit d0d8d73bcf76f94510c8309ce08841d8034aa00f (2026-11-12 12:44:11 JST, the card's Mac table, MEASUREMENTS.md and litertlm_manifest.json; main at the read); the Hub's LFS oid equals artifact_sha256 and its size 3507963904 B (anonymous API read 2026-11-12 12:51:37 JST).
quantization: int4 blockwise-32 decoder weights (the output layer included) with one scale per block, every block scale at or above 2^-14 (ai-edge-quantizer 0.10.0); int8 token embedder (one scale per output channel); float16 vision encoder; float32 activations declared for the decoder; the decoder's KV-cache writes and attention products as GPU composites (odml.cache_update, odml.runtime_bmm); fast_vlm at 512 x 512 (256 image tokens), 10,244-wide image rows (Qwen3-VL DeepStack), KV cache 2048; LiteRT external weights since 2026-11-12: the decoder's and the token embedder's weights in TFLiteWeights sections at the end of the file, the vision encoder and adapter keep theirs in the graph (the same weight bytes as the earlier file; an Android GPU needs LiteRT-LM 0.19.0 or later, LiteRT-LM#3986)
